title: routing: instrument structured fallback_reason enums (taxonomy + metrics)
author: Mina Haddad
description: ## Summary Adds a structured `fallback_reason` enum to the smart router and emits it consistently in logs and metrics. This is a prerequisite for Incident Taxonomy v1 (Routing/Fallback misbehavior vs Capacity/Fleet shortage vs Health/Region failure, etc.) and is intended to reduce ambiguity during live incidents and improve reporting. This PR does **not** change routing policy semantics; it only records why a fallback was taken (or attempted) and surfaces that signal end-to-end. ## Motivation Today, when we see a spike in fallbacks, the router only exposes freeform strings in debug logs and a coarse counter (`router_fallback_total{model=...}`). During incidents we repeatedly debate: is this a capacity issue, a healthcheck issue, a policy misconfig, or timeouts? Taxonomy rollout requires a stable, low-cardinality reason signal that can be mapped to incident types/subtypes and used by incident-bot heuristics and dashboards. ## Design ### New enum `FallbackReason` (stable allowlist) Introduces `FallbackReason` with an intentionally small set of values (low cardinality): - `CAPACITY` (no eligible capacity for target / saturation / queue full) - `UPSTREAM_HEALTH` (health gating: model/endpoint marked unhealthy, circuit open, region marked degraded) - `POLICY` (explicit policy constraint: tenant pinning, region pinning, allow/deny lists, compliance routing) - `TIMEOUT` (router timed out waiting for selection/health/capacity signal) - `COMPATIBILITY` (requested model/variant incompatible with request requirements) - `RATE_LIMIT` (router-level or preflight throttling causing fallback path) - `UNKNOWN` (default when reason cannot be determined) Notes: `RATE_LIMIT` is included because it shows up operationally as "fallback to smaller model" in some configs; we want to separate it from fleet capacity. `UNKNOWN` is expected during the rollout window and should shrink as we wire more decision points. ### Where it is set - Router selection path now sets a single primary `fallback_reason` when we choose a non-primary backend/model/region due to a gating condition. - For multi-step selection where multiple gates fail (e.g., policy rejects region A, then region B is unhealthy, then we land in region C), we record: `fallback_reason_primary` (first gate that forced fallback off the preferred target) and `fallback_reason_terminal` (final gate immediately preceding the selected target). For metrics we only emit `fallback_reason_terminal` to keep label cardinality bounded and interpretation simpler. Both are included in structured logs for deeper forensics. ### Telemetry surfaces - Structured log field: `router.fallback_reason` (`string`) and `router.fallback_reason_terminal` (`string`) - Metric counter: `router_fallback_total{fallback_reason=<enum>, route=<route_group>, tier=<hosted|dedicated|private>}` - Metric counter: `router_fallback_attempt_total{fallback_reason=<enum>, outcome=<selected|no_eligible_targets|error>}` - Trace attribute (if tracing enabled): `routing.fallback_reason` Taxonomy mapping guidance is included in code comments and in `docs/internal/reliability/incident-taxonomy-mapping.md` to avoid freeform reinterpretation. ## Taxonomy mapping notes (v1) These are guidance only; incident classification remains an on-call action. - `CAPACITY` -> typically aligns with **Capacity / Fleet shortage** (subtype: regional capacity / provisioning lag / saturation) - `UPSTREAM_HEALTH` -> typically aligns with **Region failover / health gating** or **Serving dependency unhealthy** depending on what was marked unhealthy - `POLICY` -> often aligns with **Routing policy / fallback misbehavior** (misconfig) or "expected behavior" if policy is intentional; incidents should be filed only if unexpected or customer-impacting - `TIMEOUT` -> often aligns with **Control plane / routing latency regressions** (if selection/health calls are slow) - `COMPATIBILITY` -> often aligns with **Rollout/config regression** or **Request validation** issues (depending on source) - `RATE_LIMIT` -> aligns with **Overload / throttling** (distinguish from CAPACITY) - `UNKNOWN` -> use **Unknown/Needs triage** during incident; follow-up action is to improve instrumentation at the missing decision point. ## Implementation details - Adds enum to `routing-core` and threads it through `SelectionResult` so it is available wherever we emit metrics/logs. - Converts existing ad-hoc fallback logging to structured logging. - Adds unit tests for reason assignment in the most common routes: capacity exhaustion, unhealthy region, explicit deny-policy, selection timeout. - Adds a small translation shim for older components that still send freeform reason strings; those map to `UNKNOWN` until follow-up PRs wire the exact gates. ## Files / areas changed (high level) - `services/router/src/selection/selector.ts` (assign reasons at gating points) - `services/router/src/telemetry/metrics.ts` (new counters + label guardrails) - `services/router/src/telemetry/logging.ts` (structured log fields) - `packages/routing-core/src/types.ts` (enum + docs) - `docs/internal/reliability/incident-taxonomy-mapping.md` (mapping guidance; internal) - `services/router/test/fallback_reason.test.ts` (new coverage) Illustrative snippet (selector): `if (capacity.isSaturated(target)) return fallback({ reason: FallbackReason.CAPACITY, ... }); if (!health.isHealthy(target)) return fallback({ reason: FallbackReason.UPSTREAM_HEALTH, ... }); if (!policy.allows(target, req)) return fallback({ reason: FallbackReason.POLICY, ... });` ## Metrics / cardinality constraints - `fallback_reason` is an enum allowlist, enforced by type system + runtime validation (unknown values coerce to `UNKNOWN`). - `route` label uses existing `route_group` (already bounded) rather than raw route IDs. - `tier` uses existing bounded tier tag. - This PR intentionally does **not** add model name as a label to these new counters (too high cardinality). Model-level breakdown will be derived from logs/traces when needed. ## Rollout plan - Merge behind a feature flag: `router.telemetry.fallback_reason_v1` (default ON in staging, OFF in prod initially). - After merge: enable in one hosted region for 24h and validate dashboard shape + log volume; then ramp to all regions. - Follow-up: wire incident-bot heuristic to prefer suggesting incident types when `fallback_reason != UNKNOWN` (tracked in ENG-4824/ENG-4822). ## Testing - Unit: new routing selection tests - Integration: router telemetry integration tests validate metric emission and label values - Manual: replayed a known capacity-saturation scenario in staging and verified `CAPACITY` increments and structured logs appear with expected fields ## Reviewer notes / conversation - Allison (Observability): requested avoiding model label and keeping a strict allowlist; also asked to clarify whether we emit both primary/terminal reasons in metrics. Updated to emit terminal only and added a comment + validation that coerces unknowns to `UNKNOWN`. - Ravi (Routing): asked to ensure this doesn’t change selection behavior; confirmed no functional changes and added a regression test asserting selected targets are unchanged vs baseline for representative fixtures. - Aisha (SRE): asked to include taxonomy mapping guidance somewhere durable; added `docs/internal/reliability/incident-taxonomy-mapping.md` and inline mapping comments next to the enum definition. - Ethan (Control plane): asked for a plan to map timeout reasons to control-plane vs router CPU stalls; added a note in docs that `TIMEOUT` is a symptom and will be split in v1.1 only if we can do so without increasing cardinality. ## CI - buildkite/redwood: build (pass) - buildkite/redwood: unit tests (pass) - buildkite/redwood: lint (pass) - buildkite/redwood: router integration suite (pass) ## Merge Squash merged to `main`.
release_notes: Internal: Router emits `fallback_reason` telemetry (enum) for taxonomy/dashboards; no customer-facing behavior change.
